title: Samuel prophesies
summary: Samuel prophesies to the people and announces a sign five years hence: the Son of God will come to redeem believers.

explicit_facts.text: Samuel prophesies further things and gives a sign concerning the Son of God coming in five years.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Samuel is speaking to an audience.
unspecified_visual_details: The audience's appearance, size, and exact location.

spoken_dialogue.text: Behold, I give unto you a sign;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Samuel the Lamanite

spoken_dialogue.text: for five years more cometh,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Samuel the Lamanite

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The prophecy concerns the future, not an event occurring in this scene.
prohibited_inventions: Depicting the Son of God visibly in this scene.

title: Signs of the birth
summary: Samuel describes the light that will mark the night before the Son of God is born and foretells a new star.

explicit_facts.text: Samuel foretells great lights in heaven, a night without darkness, and a new star as signs of the Son of God's coming.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Samuel speaks while an imagined celestial illustration may accompany the prophecy.
unspecified_visual_details: The specific arrangement, colors, and appearance of the lights and star.

spoken_dialogue.text: there shall be great lights in heaven,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Samuel the Lamanite

spoken_dialogue.text: And behold, there shall a new star arise,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Samuel the Lamanite

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These are future signs described in speech, not present events.
prohibited_inventions: Showing the foretold signs as happening in the present.

title: Signs and belief
summary: Samuel foretells signs and wonders in heaven, the people's amazement, and everlasting life for those who believe on the Son of God.

explicit_facts.text: Samuel foretells signs and wonders in heaven and says the people will be amazed and fall to the earth.
Whoever believes on the Son of God will have everlasting life.

unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of the signs and wonders.

spoken_dialogue.text: there shall be many signs and wonders in heaven.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Samuel the Lamanite

spoken_dialogue.text: whosoever shall believe on the Son of God,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Samuel the Lamanite

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The signs and the listeners' reaction are foretold, not shown as present events.
prohibited_inventions: Depicting supernatural signs as currently occurring.

title: Samuel's commission
summary: Samuel says the Lord commanded him through an angel to prophesy and call the people to repent. He says they are angry with him and have cast him out.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord commanded Samuel through an angel to come and prophesy, including a call to repent and prepare the way of the Lord.
Samuel says the people are angry with him and seek to destroy him, and have cast him out from among them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Samuel speaks of his rejection by the people.
unspecified_visual_details: Where the casting out occurred and whether anyone else is present now.

spoken_dialogue.text: repent and prepare the way of the Lord.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Samuel the Lamanite

spoken_dialogue.text: and have cast me out from among you.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Samuel the Lamanite

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The angel is mentioned in Samuel's account but is not described as visibly present.
prohibited_inventions: Showing the angel or staging the casting out as a current event.

title: On the city walls
summary: The speaker says he has come up upon the city walls so his listeners might hear and know of the judgments of God awaiting them because of their iniquities and the conditions of repentance. He also wants them to know of the coming of Jesus Christ and its signs so they might believe on his name.

explicit_facts.text: The speaker says he has come up upon the walls of the city.
He wants his listeners to hear and know of the judgments of God awaiting them because of their iniquities, and to know the conditions of repentance.
He wants them to know of the coming of Jesus Christ and its signs so they might believe on his name.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The speaker can be shown on the city walls while speaking.
unspecified_visual_details: The city's architecture and the listeners' appearance.

spoken_dialogue.text: have I come up upon the walls of this city,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Samuel the Lamanite

spoken_dialogue.text: that ye might hear and know of the judgments of God which do await you because of your iniquities,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Samuel the Lamanite

spoken_dialogue.text: And also that ye might know of the coming of Jesus Christ,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Samuel the Lamanite

spoken_dialogue.text: and that ye might know of the signs of his coming,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Samuel the Lamanite

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The judgments await the listeners because of their iniquities; Jesus Christ and the signs of his coming are spoken of, not described as visibly present.

Depicting Jesus Christ or signs of his coming as present events.

title: Belief and repentance
summary: Samuel teaches that belief in Christ leads to repentance and remission of sins through Christ's merits.

explicit_facts.text: Those who believe on Christ's name will repent of their sins and may receive remission through his merits.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Samuel continues speaking from the city wall.

spoken_dialogue.text: ye will repent of all your sins,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Samuel the Lamanite

spoken_dialogue.text: a remission of them through his merits.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Samuel the Lamanite

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse gives a teaching, not a visible event.
prohibited_inventions: Depicting remission as a visible supernatural action.

title: The sign of his death
summary: Samuel introduces a sign of Christ's death and teaches that Christ must die so salvation and resurrection may come.

explicit_facts.text: Samuel gives a sign of Christ's death and says Christ must die for salvation and the resurrection of the dead, bringing people into the Lord's presence.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Samuel continues his address from the city wall.
unspecified_visual_details: Any visual representation accompanying the teaching.

spoken_dialogue.text: a sign of his death.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Samuel the Lamanite

spoken_dialogue.text: he surely must die that salvation may come;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Samuel the Lamanite

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Christ's death and resurrection are taught as future events; do not stage them here.
prohibited_inventions: Depicting Christ's death or resurrection as currently happening.

title: Redemption and the second death
summary: Samuel teaches that Christ's death and resurrection redeem mankind and bring people back into the Lord's presence. He warns the people to repent to avoid condemnation and the second death.

explicit_facts.text: Christ's death brings resurrection and redeems mankind from spiritual death; Christ's resurrection brings mankind back into the Lord's presence.
Samuel teaches that repentance avoids the second death and warns the people to repent lest they come under condemnation.

unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of spiritual death, condemnation, or fire.

spoken_dialogue.text: the resurrection of Christ redeemeth mankind,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Samuel the Lamanite

spoken_dialogue.text: repent ye, repent ye,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Samuel the Lamanite

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Fire and being hewn down are figures of judgment in Samuel's teaching, not a narrated visible event.
prohibited_inventions: Literalizing the metaphor of being hewn down and cast into fire.

title: Darkness at Christ's death
summary: Samuel foretells that at Christ's death the sun, moon, and stars will give no light, and darkness will cover the land for three days until Christ rises.

explicit_facts.text: Samuel foretells three days without light on the land, beginning when Christ suffers death and ending when he rises from the dead.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Samuel describes the future darkness in speech.
unspecified_visual_details: The landscape and precise appearance of the darkness.

spoken_dialogue.text: the sun shall be darkened
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Samuel the Lamanite

spoken_dialogue.text: for the space of three days,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Samuel the Lamanite

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is a future sign described by Samuel, not a present event.
prohibited_inventions: Showing the land currently in darkness.

title: Thunder and broken rocks
summary: Samuel foretells thunder, lightning, an earthquake, and rocks breaking apart across the earth when Christ yields up the ghost.

explicit_facts.text: At Christ's death, thunder and lightning will last many hours, the earth will shake, and rocks will break apart into seams, cracks, and fragments.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Samuel describes the foretold events as speech.
unspecified_visual_details: The precise terrain and scale of the described damage.

spoken_dialogue.speaker: Samuel the Lamanite

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The destruction is a future sign, not a present event.
prohibited_inventions: Showing the foretold earthquake or rock damage occurring now.

title: Tempests and changed terrain
summary: Samuel foretells great tempests, mountains lowered or raised, broken highways, and cities becoming desolate.

explicit_facts.text: Samuel foretells tempests, mountains laid low, valleys becoming high mountains, highways broken up, and cities becoming desolate.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Samuel continues his prophecy from the city wall.
unspecified_visual_details: Which mountains, highways, and cities are meant, and what they look like.

title: Graves and saints foretold

explicit_facts.text: Many graves shall be opened and yield up many of their dead.
Many saints shall appear unto many.

unspecified_visual_details: Who speaks the words and where.
The appearance of the graves, the dead, and the saints.

title: The angel's message
summary: Samuel says an angel told him that thunder, lightning, tempest, and three days of darkness would accompany the signs, and that many would see greater things and believe.

explicit_facts.text: Samuel says an angel told him there would be thunder, lightning, tempest, and darkness over the whole earth for three days.
The angel said many would see greater things so they might believe the signs and wonders would come to pass throughout the land.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Samuel recounts what the angel said.
unspecified_visual_details: The angel's appearance and the greater signs.

title: Belief and judgment
summary: Samuel teaches that those who believe may be saved, while those who do not believe face righteous judgment. He urges the people to remember their freedom to choose good or evil, life or death.

explicit_facts.text: Samuel teaches that believers may be saved and that those who do not believe may receive righteous judgment.
Samuel says people are free to act for themselves and choose life or death, good or evil.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Samuel concludes his address to the people.
